title: Xanthe and the Witness
premise: Rosalind Underhill, the coroner of Marrow Creek, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, until a confession letter arrives for a drowning they closed a decade ago: the death of their own brother, Danny. The letter's author is dying and wants absolution, but naming him means dismantling the official story that Rosalind's found family—the retired sheriff who raised them—helped build to protect someone else. As the statute of limitations ticks down, Rosalind must choose between the law that failed them and the people who became their family, and in the end they publish the truth themselves, losing the sheriff's trust but gaining a chosen family that can survive honesty.
about_author: Astrid Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing small-town confessions before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much and say too little, from a farmhouse she shares with two unsociable cats.

chapters.title: The Postmark
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Three weeks after burying old Tom Vess, Rosalind receives a confession letter postmarked the day after his funeral, admitting Tom's 'accidental' drowning was murder—and hinting it wasn't the writer's first. The handwriting unsettles Rosalind for reasons they can't name. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in curiosity, as the quiet life of invisible corrections begins to crack open.

chapters.title: What the Sheriff Knew
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Following the letter's clues, Rosalind reopens Danny Underhill's decade-old drowning and finds gaps in the file only one person could have left: Amos Pell, the retired sheriff who took them in after Danny died. Confronting him, Rosalind learns Amos helped close the case to shield someone he loved. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve as duty and love split apart.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. With eleven days before the statute expires, Rosalind tracks the letter's author to a hospice ward: Walter Finch, Danny's best friend, who confesses to a drunken prank gone wrong while Amos's own son watched and ran. But Finch dies overnight, leaving no admissible statement, and someone ransacks Rosalind's office for the letter. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At Danny's grave, with the town gathered for its rededication, Rosalind reads Finch's letter aloud and names the truth—including Amos's cover-up—choosing justice outside the law over silence. Amos walks away; half the town stays, becoming the family Rosalind never let themselves have. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging, as Rosalind finally stops being invisible.
